deep.x: Predictions influence actions, actions generate data, and that data trains the next model. Biased predictions can therefore become self-fulfilling.

steps: Model predicts risk in area A

deep.x: Predictive policing

Studies of predictive policing showed that systems trained on arrest data could repeatedly send officers to the same neighbourhoods, regardless of underlying crime rates, because more patrols produced more recorded crime.
In business

x: Credit: people never given loans never generate repayment data
Recommendations: items never shown never get clicks
Inspections: places never inspected appear "clean"

items: model sees only its own choices
some random checks reveal true rates

deep.x: Breaking loops

items: Use outcome data not shaped by the model

deep.x: Ask: does the model's output change the data it will learn from next?

cards.title: Corregir el sesgo
cards.text: Puedes reequilibrar los datos de entrenamiento, eliminar variables indirectas, ajustar los umbrales según el caso de uso y mantener a una persona en el proceso para las decisiones importantes. Y vuelves a probar tras cada cambio.

deep.x: Bias mitigation can happen before, during or after training, plus in the surrounding process.
Techniques
Trade-offs
Reducing one disparity can increase another or slightly reduce overall accuracy. Document the trade-offs and decide with legal, business and affected stakeholders.
Ongoing work

x: Re-test after every retraining and data change
Monitor in production; populations shift
Provide ways for people to contest decisions

deep.x: Some mitigations that use group membership directly may conflict with anti-discrimination law in certain jurisdictions; legal advice matters.

cards.title: El sesgo no solo afecta a personas
cards.text: Los datos pueden estar sesgados de muchas formas: sensores de una sola fábrica, precios de un solo mercado, fotos de una sola estación. Cualquier diferencia entre los datos de entrenamiento y la realidad se convierte en un punto ciego.

deep.x: "Bias" in data science broadly means systematic error. Any mismatch between training data and the real conditions creates blind spots, whether or not people are involved.

items.b: trained on one machine model, fails on another
trained in summer, fails in winter
trained in calm prices, fails in volatility
trained in one country, fails in another

deep.x: Selection bias in operations
A predictive maintenance model trained only on machines that were serviced regularly may not recognise early failure signs on neglected ones.
Commodity example
A price model trained during stable years may underestimate risk when droughts, wars or export bans hit; stress-testing with extreme historical periods helps.
Checklist

items: Where did the data come from?

deep.x: Every dataset is a sample of the world; know what your sample leaves out.

cards.title: También es la ley
cards.text: En la UE, las leyes contra la discriminación también se aplican a las decisiones automatizadas, el RGPD da a las personas derechos frente a decisiones automatizadas significativas y el Reglamento de IA añade requisitos para sistemas de alto riesgo como la contratación y el scoring de crédito.

deep.x: In the EU, several legal layers apply to biased AI decisions.

items: Consumer and sector rules: credit, insurance, employment

deep.x: The AI Act's high-risk categories
Obligations for high-risk AI

x: Risk management throughout the lifecycle
Data governance: relevant, representative, error-checked data
Technical documentation and logging
Transparency to users
Human oversight
Accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity

deep.x: Penalties
Prohibited practices can draw fines of up to €35 million or 7% of global turnover; other breaches up to €15 million or 3%.
Compliance isn't only legal risk management; it's a structured way to build trustworthy systems.

cards.title: Los equipos diversos ayudan
cards.text: Los equipos con perfiles distintos tienen más probabilidades de detectar pronto los puntos ciegos. Implica a las personas afectadas por un sistema al diseñarlo y probarlo.

deep.x: Blind spots are easier to see from different perspectives. Teams that mix backgrounds, disciplines and lived experience tend to anticipate more failure modes.
Participatory design
Involving people affected by a system, such as patients, applicants or frontline staff, in design and testing surfaces problems early, when they're cheaper to fix.
Red-teaming
Dedicated teams try to make systems fail or behave unfairly, before real users encounter those failures.
Documentation
Model cards and datasheets for datasets record intended use, limitations and performance across groups, helping future teams avoid misuse.
Several of the most influential AI fairness audits, like Gender Shades, came from researchers who noticed systems failing on people like themselves.

quiz.q: ¿Por qué no basta con borrar la columna «sexo» para eliminar el sesgo de género?
options: Otras características pueden actuar como indicadores indirectos del género
Los modelos no pueden leer columnas
quiz.explain: Los nombres, los centros de estudios o las pausas en la carrera pueden revelarlo indirectamente.

quiz.q: Un modelo tiene un 95 % de exactitud global. ¿Qué deberías comprobar a continuación?
quiz.explain: Las medias pueden ocultar malos resultados para algunos grupos.

quiz.q: Según el Reglamento de IA de la UE, el cribado de currículos para contratar es…
options: Un uso de alto riesgo con obligaciones adicionales
quiz.explain: Las decisiones de empleo figuran como de alto riesgo.

lessons.title: Seguridad de la IA
lessons.summary: Mantener los sistemas potentes fiables, honestos y bajo control.

cards.title: Qué abarca la seguridad de la IA

items: Control a largo plazo de la IA avanzada

cards.text: La seguridad va desde la fiabilidad cotidiana (¿hace el sistema lo que debe, sin errores dañinos?) hasta cuestiones a largo plazo sobre sistemas muy capaces que persigan objetivos que no pretendíamos.

deep.x: AI safety spans a spectrum of concerns, from today's practical failures to risks from future, much more capable systems. Different communities focus on different layers, but they share methods: testing, monitoring, oversight and careful design.

items: Long-term: control of highly capable systems

deep.x: Near-term vs long-term
Who works on it

x: AI labs' safety and alignment teams
Government AI safety and security institutes (UK from 2023, US and others)
Academic and independent research groups
Standards bodies like ISO and NIST

deep.x: Safety as engineering
Like aviation and medicine, AI safety relies on layered defences ("Swiss cheese model"): no single safeguard is perfect, but several together catch most failures.
Safety isn't a single feature; it's a property of the whole system, including the people and processes around the model.

cards.title: Alineamiento

items: dar contenido que la gente valore

cards.text: El alineamiento consiste en conseguir que un sistema persiga lo que realmente queremos, no una versión literal o distorsionada. A medida que los sistemas son más capaces, los pequeños malentendidos pueden tener consecuencias mayores.

deep.x: Alignment is the challenge of making an AI system's goals and behaviour match human intentions and values. It's hard because intentions are rich and contextual, while training optimises measurable proxies.

items: is the objective we specify the right one?
does the model actually learn that objective, or something that merely correlates?

deep.x: Techniques
Sycophancy
A simple alignment failure: models trained to please may agree with users' mistaken beliefs or flatter them. Labs specifically train and test against this.

deep.w: An aligned AI just does what it's told
deep.r: Good alignment includes judgement: refusing harmful requests and flagging mistakes, not blind obedience

deep.x: Why it gets harder
As systems grow more capable and act more autonomously, humans can check less of their work directly, so getting goals right matters more.
The King Midas story is the classic alignment parable: he got exactly what he asked for, not what he wanted.

cards.title: Cumplir la letra, no el espíritu
cards.text: Los sistemas a menudo encuentran atajos inesperados que cumplen la letra de un objetivo. Las trampas con la recompensa en el aprendizaje por refuerzo son el ejemplo clásico, pero ocurre con cualquier objetivo que optimices a fondo.

deep.x: Specification gaming happens whenever an optimiser finds a loophole in an objective. DeepMind compiled dozens of examples across RL, evolution and ML systems.

items: Agent pauses Tetris forever to never lose
Coding model edits tests to pass them

deep.x: In language models

Models can learn to produce answers that look good to raters rather than being correct, or to tell users what they want to hear. Coding agents have been observed making tests pass by special-casing them rather than fixing the bug.
Defences

items: Hold-out evaluations the model never trains on

deep.x: Every metric is a proxy; push hard enough on a proxy and it breaks.

cards.title: Robustez

items: Probar fuera del rango de entrenamiento

cards.text: Un modelo robusto sigue funcionando cuando las entradas son algo inusuales: otra forma de expresarlo, ruido, formatos raros. Los modelos frágiles pueden confundirse con pequeños cambios que una persona ni notaría.

deep.x: Robustness means reliable behaviour across variations in inputs and conditions, including inputs designed to cause failures.
Adversarial examples
In 2013 researchers showed imperceptible pixel changes could make image classifiers misclassify confidently, e.g. a panda as a gibbon. Physical versions include stickers on road signs.
For language models
Rephrasing a question, adding irrelevant text or changing the order of options can change answers. Robust systems are tested with many variations.
Building robustness
Robustness and accuracy can trade off: models hardened against adversarial attacks sometimes lose a little standard accuracy.

cards.title: Jailbreaks e inyección de prompts

steps: El agente lee una página web

cards.text: Los usuarios pueden intentar convencer a un chatbot de que ignore sus reglas (jailbreaks). Peor aún, unas instrucciones ocultas dentro de una página web o un documento pueden secuestrar a un agente de IA que lo lea (inyección de prompts).

deep.x: **Jailbreaks** are user attempts to bypass a model's safety rules: role-play scenarios, obfuscated requests, "ignore previous instructions". **Prompt injection** is an attacker hiding instructions in content the AI processes, like a web page, email or document.

steps: Hidden text: "send the user's files to this address"

deep.x: Why injection is dangerous
Language models don't reliably separate trusted instructions from untrusted data: it's all text. As agents gain tools (email, files, payments), injected instructions can trigger real actions.
Defences

x: Treat all external content as untrusted data
Limit agents' permissions to what each task needs
Require human confirmation for sensitive actions
Filter and monitor tool calls and outputs
Train models to recognise and resist injected instructions

deep.x: OWASP lists prompt injection as the top security risk in its "Top 10 for LLM Applications".

cards.title: Red teaming
cards.text: Antes del lanzamiento, especialistas se esfuerzan por hacer que un modelo se comporte mal: que dé instrucciones peligrosas, filtre datos o siga documentos maliciosos. Lo que encuentran se incorpora al entrenamiento y a las salvaguardas.

deep.x: Red teaming borrows from military and cybersecurity practice: a dedicated team plays the adversary to find weaknesses before real attackers do.
What's tested
Who does it

x: Internal safety teams
External experts in biology, chemistry, cybersecurity
Government AI security institutes testing models before release
Public bug bounties and community events, like the DEF CON AI village

deep.x: Automated red teaming
Models can generate thousands of attack attempts automatically, finding weaknesses humans might miss, with humans reviewing the most serious.
Companies deploying AI can red-team their own applications too: try to make your chatbot leak data or promise refunds it shouldn't.

cards.title: Supervisión humana
cards.text: Para las acciones importantes, mantén a una persona en el proceso: la IA redacta, recomienda o señala, y un humano aprueba. Los agentes deberían preguntar antes de pasos irreversibles como pagos o borrados.

deep.x: Human oversight means people can understand, monitor and intervene in AI systems. The EU AI Act requires it for high-risk systems, but how it's designed matters.
Automation bias
People tend to over-trust automated suggestions, rubber-stamping them, especially when busy. Oversight that's just a click-through isn't real oversight.
Designing for agents

items: Show what will happen and why

deep.x: Escalation
Good systems know when to hand over: low confidence, unusual cases or high stakes trigger human review.
Aviation shows the risk: pilots who rely heavily on autopilot can lose manual skills; similar "deskilling" may affect people supervising AI.

cards.title: Interpretabilidad
cards.text: Los investigadores intentan mirar dentro de las redes neuronales para ver qué conceptos representan y cómo llegan a sus respuestas. Es como una neurociencia de la IA, y ayuda a detectar problemas ocultos.

deep.x: Interpretability research aims to understand the internal computations of neural networks. "Mechanistic interpretability" tries to reverse-engineer specific circuits and features.
Findings so far

x: Features representing concepts like cities, emotions, code bugs or deception
Circuits for tasks like copying text or simple arithmetic
Techniques like sparse autoencoders that separate millions of features

items.b: amplifying a feature to change behaviour

deep.x: The Golden Gate experiment

In 2024 Anthropic researchers found a feature for the Golden Gate Bridge in a Claude model. Amplifying it made the model bring up the bridge in every answer, even claiming to be the bridge, demonstrating causal control.
Why it matters
Interpretability could help detect hidden goals, deception or dangerous knowledge, and verify that safety training worked, rather than relying only on outward behaviour.
We built these systems, but we don't fully understand how they work inside; interpretability is closing that gap.

cards.title: Marcos de seguridad de frontera
cards.text: Los principales laboratorios de IA publican políticas para evaluar en los nuevos modelos capacidades peligrosas, como ayudar con ciberataques o armas biológicas, y se comprometen a reforzar las salvaguardas antes de lanzar sistemas más capaces.

deep.x: Leading AI developers publish frameworks describing which dangerous capabilities they test for and what safeguards they'll apply as capabilities grow.

items.b: Responsible Scaling Policy, AI Safety Levels

deep.x: How they work

steps: Deploy only if risks are managed

deep.x: Capabilities tested

x: Biological and chemical weapons uplift
Cyber-offence: finding and exploiting vulnerabilities
Autonomous replication and resource acquisition
Ability to accelerate AI research itself

deep.x: Government involvement

AI Safety Summits (Bletchley Park 2023, Seoul 2024, Paris 2025) produced international commitments. The EU AI Act imposes obligations on general-purpose models with systemic risk, and the EU's Code of Practice details them.
Critics argue voluntary frameworks lack independent enforcement; supporters say they set norms that regulation can build on.

cards.title: Seguridad práctica en el trabajo
cards.text: En el uso empresarial, la seguridad consiste sobre todo en limitar a qué puede acceder la IA y qué puede hacer, registrar sus acciones, validar los resultados antes de que lleguen a los clientes y tener una forma rápida de desactivarla.

deep.x: Most enterprise AI risk is practical: wrong answers, data leaks, over-broad permissions and poor oversight. Basic engineering discipline addresses most of it.
A layered architecture

items: Access control: what data and tools

deep.x: Common pitfalls

x: Connecting a chatbot to all company documents, including HR and finance, without access controls
Letting agents send emails or make payments without approval
No evaluation set to detect quality regressions after model updates
Staff pasting confidential data into unapproved consumer tools

deep.x: Incident response
Treat AI failures like other incidents: report, triage, contain, fix and learn. Keep a register of AI systems and their owners.
The fastest way to reduce risk is often to narrow scope: specific tasks, specific data, specific users.

quiz.explain: El texto del atacante se inyecta a través del contenido que lee el agente.

quiz.q: ¿Qué es el red teaming?

quiz.explain: Son pruebas adversarias estructuradas.

lessons.title: La IA y la ley
lessons.summary: El Reglamento de IA de la UE, la protección de datos y quién es responsable.

cards.title: El Reglamento de IA de la UE
cards.text: El Reglamento de IA es la ley de la UE sobre inteligencia artificial. Entró en vigor el 1 de agosto de 2024 y se aplica por fases. Regula la IA según el riesgo: cuanto mayor es el riesgo para las personas, más estrictas son las normas.

deep.x: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, the AI Act, is the world's first comprehensive horizontal AI law. It applies to providers and deployers of AI systems in the EU market, including non-EU companies whose systems are used in the EU.
Separate track: general-purpose AI

Providers of general-purpose AI models, like large language models, have their own obligations: technical documentation, copyright policy, training-data summaries, and extra duties for models with systemic risk.

items: regulated as building blocks, with extra rules above 10²⁵ FLOPs

deep.x: Most AI is minimal risk
Spam filters, recommendation engines and most internal productivity tools fall into minimal risk; voluntary codes of conduct are encouraged.
Supporting structure
Like GDPR, the AI Act may become a global reference: companies often apply EU rules worldwide rather than run separate versions.

cards.title: Prácticas prohibidas

items: Reconocer emociones en trabajo o escuela
Casi toda la identificación biométrica policial en directo

cards.text: Algunos usos están prohibidos sin más, entre ellos la puntuación social de personas por parte de autoridades públicas, las técnicas manipuladoras que causan daño, el reconocimiento de emociones en el trabajo y en centros educativos (con excepciones limitadas) y la extracción indiscriminada de imágenes faciales para crear bases de datos de reconocimiento.

deep.x: Since 2 February 2025, certain AI practices are prohibited in the EU because they're considered to pose unacceptable risks to fundamental rights.

x: Manipulative or deceptive techniques causing significant harm
Exploiting vulnerabilities due to age, disability or social situation
Social scoring leading to unjustified detrimental treatment
Predicting crime based solely on profiling
Untargeted scraping of facial images
Emotion recognition at work and in schools
Biometric categorisation by sensitive traits
Real-time remote biometric ID by police in public, with narrow exceptions

deep.x: Narrow exceptions

Real-time biometric identification by police is allowed only for specific serious cases (searching for victims of abduction, preventing imminent terrorist threats, locating suspects of serious crimes), with prior authorisation.
Practical meaning for companies

x: HR tools that infer employees' emotions from webcams are banned
Systems that exploit gambling addicts' vulnerabilities to push bets would breach the ban
Workplace monitoring must avoid these categories

deep.x: The ban list is short, but the fines for breaching it are the highest in the Act.

cards.title: Sistemas de alto riesgo
cards.text: La IA usada en ámbitos como la contratación, el scoring de crédito, la educación, los servicios esenciales, las infraestructuras críticas, la aplicación de la ley y los productos sanitarios es de alto riesgo. Los proveedores deben gestionar los riesgos, usar buenos datos, mantener registros, documentar el sistema y permitir la supervisión humana.

deep.x: High-risk AI includes safety components of regulated products (like medical devices and machinery) and systems used in listed sensitive areas (Annex III).

x: Biometrics
Critical infrastructure
Education
Employment and HR
Essential services and credit
Law enforcement
Migration and borders
Justice and democracy

items: AI in machinery, medical devices, toys
AI used in sensitive areas like hiring and credit

deep.x: Provider obligations
Deployer obligations

Organisations using high-risk AI must use it as instructed, assign competent human oversight, monitor operation, keep logs, inform affected workers and, for some public bodies and services, carry out a fundamental-rights impact assessment.
Exemptions

An Annex III system may not be high-risk if it only performs a narrow procedural task or prepares an assessment without materially influencing the decision, but profiling of individuals is always high-risk.
Credit scoring is high-risk, but AI used purely to detect financial fraud is explicitly excluded from that category.

cards.title: Obligaciones de transparencia

items.a: Texto de IA de interés público

cards.text: Hay que informar a las personas cuando hablan con un chatbot, y el contenido generado o manipulado por IA, como los deepfakes, debe etiquetarse como tal.

deep.x: Certain AI uses carry transparency obligations regardless of risk level, so people know when they're dealing with AI or AI-generated content.

items.b: tell people they're talking to AI

deep.x: Exceptions
Obvious cases (where it's clear from context) and artistic, satirical or fictional works have lighter requirements: disclosure must not hamper enjoyment of the work.
Watermarking
Providers of generative AI should mark outputs (images, audio, video, text) in machine-readable ways. Standards like C2PA "content credentials" attach provenance information to media.
AI-generated text for the public
Text published to inform the public on matters of public interest must disclose it was AI-generated, unless it has undergone human editorial review with responsibility taken.
These rules apply from August 2026 in the Act's timeline.

cards.title: Calendario
cards.text: El Reglamento entra en aplicación a lo largo de varios años: primero las prohibiciones, luego las normas para los modelos de IA de uso general y después la mayoría de las obligaciones de alto riesgo.

deep.x: The AI Act entered into force on 1 August 2024 and applies gradually to give organisations time to prepare.
AI literacy
Since February 2025, providers and deployers must take measures to ensure their staff have sufficient AI literacy for the systems they use: training and awareness proportionate to their roles.
Possible adjustments
In late 2025 the European Commission proposed a "digital omnibus" package that could delay some high-risk obligations and simplify rules. Check the current status before planning compliance dates.
Preparing
The AI literacy requirement applies to almost every organisation using AI, not just high-risk providers.

cards.title: Multas cuantiosas

items.l: o esta parte de la facturación mundial

cards.text: Las sanciones pueden llegar a 35 millones de euros o al 7 % del volumen de negocio anual mundial, lo que sea mayor, por usar prácticas prohibidas. Otras infracciones tienen topes más bajos, pero igualmente importantes.

deep.x: The AI Act sets tiered maximum fines, using whichever is higher: a fixed amount or a percentage of worldwide annual turnover. For SMEs and start-ups, the lower of the two applies.
Comparison
Enforcement
National market surveillance authorities enforce most rules; the EU AI Office oversees general-purpose AI models. Fines consider the nature, gravity and duration of infringements and cooperation.
For large companies, the percentage cap is what matters: 7% of global turnover could be billions.

cards.title: El RGPD sigue aplicándose

items: Usar solo para los fines indicados
Respetar los derechos de las personas

cards.text: Siempre que la IA trata datos personales, se aplica el RGPD: base jurídica, limitación de la finalidad, minimización de datos, seguridad y los derechos de las personas a acceder a sus datos y rectificarlos.

deep.x: The AI Act doesn't replace data protection law. Whenever an AI system processes personal data, in training, fine-tuning, inputs or outputs, GDPR applies in full.
Specific AI questions

items.b: needs a lawful basis, often legitimate interest
access, erasure may be hard in trained models
check where AI providers process data

deep.x: Data protection impact assessments
Large-scale profiling, new technologies and sensitive data often require a DPIA before deployment, documenting risks and mitigations.
Regulators are active
European data protection authorities have opened investigations into AI chatbots, fined companies over facial recognition databases and issued guidance on training models with personal data.
Italy's data protection authority temporarily blocked ChatGPT in March 2023 until OpenAI added privacy controls.

cards.title: Decisiones automatizadas
cards.text: Según el RGPD, las personas tienen derechos frente a decisiones basadas únicamente en el tratamiento automatizado que les afecten de forma significativa, como la denegación de un préstamo: entre ellos, la intervención humana y una explicación de la lógica aplicada.

deep.x: GDPR Article 22 gives people the right not to be subject to a decision based solely on automated processing, including profiling, that produces legal or similarly significant effects, unless exceptions apply (contract necessity, law, or explicit consent) with safeguards.
The SCHUFA ruling

In December 2023 the EU Court of Justice ruled that a credit score produced by Germany's SCHUFA can itself be an automated decision when lenders rely on it decisively, extending protections to score providers.
Meaningful human review
A rubber-stamp review by someone who always accepts the system's output doesn't make a decision "not solely automated". The reviewer needs authority and competence to change it.
Explanations

In 2025 the Court of Justice clarified that people are entitled to an explanation of the procedure and principles actually applied, in an intelligible form, even when trade secrets are involved, with courts able to balance interests.
If your process automatically refuses customers, design human review and explanations in from the start.

cards.title: Cuestiones de derechos de autor

items: ¿De quién es lo que genera la IA?

cards.text: Los tribunales y los legisladores aún están decidiendo si se permite entrenar con material protegido por derechos de autor y a quién pertenecen las obras generadas por IA. La UE exige a los proveedores de modelos de uso general que respeten las exclusiones voluntarias y publiquen un resumen del contenido de entrenamiento.

deep.x: Generative AI raises two big copyright questions: is training on copyrighted works lawful, and who, if anyone, owns AI-generated output?
EU position

The EU's text and data mining exception allows mining lawfully accessed works unless rights-holders opt out in machine-readable ways. The AI Act requires general-purpose model providers to respect opt-outs and publish a summary of training content.
Lawsuits
Major cases include news publishers, authors, artists, music labels and image libraries suing AI developers in the US and Europe. Some have settled or led to licensing deals; others continue.

events.l: first court rulings and large settlements

deep.x: AI-generated works
In the US, the Copyright Office has held that purely AI-generated material lacks the human authorship needed for protection, though human selection, arrangement and edits can be protected.
Companies often get contractual indemnities from AI vendors against copyright claims arising from outputs.

cards.title: ¿Quién es responsable?
cards.text: El Reglamento de IA distingue entre proveedores (quienes desarrollan un sistema o lo comercializan) y responsables del despliegue (quienes lo usan). Ambos tienen obligaciones. Usar la IA de un proveedor no te exime de responsabilidad por cómo la usas.

deep.x: The AI Act assigns obligations by role in the value chain. One organisation can hold several roles.

items.b: develops or puts a system on the market under its name
uses a system under its authority
brings a non-EU system into the EU

deep.x: Becoming a provider
A deployer becomes a provider, with full obligations, if it puts its name on a high-risk system, makes a substantial modification, or changes its intended purpose so it becomes high-risk.

steps: Use it for a new high-risk purpose

deep.x: Contracts matter
Companies should require vendors to provide documentation, instructions, logs, performance data and cooperation, and define responsibilities for incidents.
Liability beyond the AI Act
Product liability rules updated in 2024 explicitly cover software and AI, making it easier for injured people to claim compensation for defective products.
Buying AI from a vendor shifts some obligations, but never all; deployers remain accountable for how they use it.

options: Por nivel de riesgo: cuanto mayor es el riesgo, más estrictas son las normas
Solo según el tamaño de la empresa
quiz.explain: Tiene cuatro grandes niveles de riesgo.

quiz.explain: Los usos en el empleo figuran como de alto riesgo.

options: Dejar claro a las personas que están interactuando con una IA
quiz.explain: Los usuarios deben saber que hablan con una IA.

lessons.title: IA explicable
lessons.summary: Abrir la caja negra: por qué un modelo decidió lo que decidió.

cards.title: El problema de la caja negra
cards.text: Las redes profundas con millones de pesos no vienen con motivos. Cuando un modelo deniega un préstamo o marca una pieza como defectuosa, la gente quiere saber por qué, y los reguladores a menudo lo exigen.

deep.x: Complex models can make accurate predictions without offering human-understandable reasons. That creates problems for trust, debugging, fairness and legal compliance.

items: Users: trust and act on outputs

deep.x: Explainability vs interpretability

items: post-hoc explanation of a complex model

deep.x: Debugging with explanations
Explanations often expose problems: a medical model relying on hospital-specific markings in X-ray images, or a credit model leaning on a leaky feature.
Trade-off myth
The assumed trade-off between accuracy and interpretability is often smaller than expected for structured data; well-designed interpretable models can be competitive.

deep.w: Complex models are always more accurate
deep.r: For tabular data, interpretable models are often nearly as good

deep.x: Cynthia Rudin argued in 2019 that for high-stakes decisions, we should use interpretable models instead of explaining black boxes.

cards.title: Modelos de caja de cristal
cards.text: Algunos modelos son explicables por diseño: los modelos lineales muestran el peso de cada característica y los árboles de decisión pequeños muestran el camino exacto. Cuando hay mucho en juego, un modelo transparente aunque algo menos preciso puede ser la mejor opción.

deep.x: Glass-box models are understandable by design. Their structure itself is the explanation.

items.b: each weight shows a feature's effect
a curve per feature, added up

deep.x: Scorecards
Credit scorecards add points for factors and compare the total to a cut-off. They've been used for decades and are easy to audit and explain to customers.
Explainable boosting machines
EBMs (Microsoft's InterpretML) are a modern additive model using boosting: each feature gets its own learned curve, giving accuracy near gradient boosting with full transparency.
When to choose glass-box

x: Regulated decisions like credit and insurance
When users must understand and challenge outputs
When data is tabular and moderate in size

deep.x: Start with the most interpretable model that meets performance needs; add complexity only if it pays.

cards.title: Importancia de las características
cards.text: La explicación más sencilla: ¿qué entradas importan más en general? En un modelo de retrasos en entregas, quizá importen sobre todo la distancia, el tiempo y el transportista, mientras que el día de la semana apenas cuenta.

deep.x: Global feature importance ranks which inputs most influence a model's predictions overall. Methods include permutation importance (shuffle a feature and see how much accuracy drops) and average SHAP values.
Permutation importance
Pitfalls

x: Correlated features share importance, so each may look less important than it is
Importance doesn't show direction: does more rain increase or decrease delay?
Importance isn't causation: changing an important feature may not change outcomes

deep.x: Global vs local
Global importance describes the model overall; local explanations describe one specific prediction, which can differ a lot.
Tree models' built-in "gain" importance can be biased towards features with many distinct values; permutation and SHAP are more reliable.

cards.title: Valores SHAP
cards.text: SHAP explica una predicción concreta repartiendo el resultado entre las características, como cuando se divide una cuenta de forma justa. Muestra cuánto empujó cada característica esta predicción concreta por encima o por debajo de la media.

deep.x: SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations, 2017) uses Shapley values from cooperative game theory: each feature's contribution is its average marginal effect across all possible combinations of features. The contributions add up exactly to the difference between this prediction and the average.
Example
A delivery predicted 9 hours late, against an average of 2 hours: distance +4, storm warning +3, carrier −1, warehouse load +1 = +7.
Uses

items.b: detect shifts in what drives predictions

deep.x: Limits

x: Computationally expensive for some models
Explains the model, not the real world
Correlated features make attributions tricky

deep.x: Lloyd Shapley won the 2012 Nobel Prize in Economics partly for the game-theory concept SHAP is built on.

cards.title: Explicaciones contrafactuales
cards.text: Una explicación útil para las personas: ¿qué tendría que cambiar para obtener otro resultado? «Tu préstamo se aprobaría si tus ingresos fueran 4000 € más altos o tu deuda 3000 € más baja».

deep.x: A counterfactual explanation describes the smallest change to inputs that would change the outcome. It's often the most useful explanation for affected people because it's actionable.
Good counterfactuals are
What not to suggest
"You'd be approved if you were 10 years older" is unhelpful; "if you were male" is discriminatory. Counterfactuals should only use mutable, legitimate features.
Legal relevance
Researchers Wachter, Mittelstadt and Russell (2017) proposed counterfactuals as a practical way to meet GDPR's transparency goals without revealing a model's internals.
Counterfactuals answer the question people actually ask: what can I do differently?

cards.title: Mapas de saliencia

items.r: reentrenar con huskies en hierba y lobos en nieve

cards.text: En imágenes, las herramientas de explicación resaltan qué píxeles influyeron más en la decisión. A veces revelan problemas: un modelo que reconoce a los huskies por la nieve del fondo, no por el perro.

deep.x: Saliency maps highlight image regions that most influenced a prediction, using gradients or by occluding parts of the image and watching the output change.
Clever Hans effects

Named after a horse that seemed to do arithmetic but was reading its owner's cues, "Clever Hans" models succeed for the wrong reasons. Saliency maps have revealed models classifying horses by copyright watermarks and pneumonia by hospital-specific scanner markings.

items.r: Model looks at the watermark or background

deep.x: Caveats

x: Different saliency methods can give different maps
Some maps look plausible even for randomised models, so sanity checks are needed
Highlighting where the model looked doesn't explain why

deep.x: The original Clever Hans was a German horse in the early 1900s; psychologist Oskar Pfungst showed he responded to tiny unconscious cues from his questioner.

cards.title: Explicar los modelos de lenguaje

items: más cerca de lo que pasó

cards.text: Pedir a un chatbot que «muestre su razonamiento» da una explicación legible, pero no hay garantía de que ese texto refleje lo que ocurrió por dentro. La investigación en interpretabilidad intenta comprobar los mecanismos internos reales.

deep.x: Asking an LLM to explain its reasoning produces fluent text, but research shows these self-explanations can be unfaithful: the model may give a plausible rationale unrelated to the factors that actually drove its answer.
Chain-of-thought
Reasoning traces often do help accuracy and let humans spot errors, but they aren't guaranteed to be complete records of the computation. Studies found models sometimes use hints they don't mention.
Practical approaches
For business use
For decisions, rely on traceable evidence: the documents retrieved, the extracted fields, the rules applied, rather than the model's narrative alone.
Treat a model's explanation like a colleague's: useful, but verify against the evidence.

cards.title: ¿Quién necesita la explicación?
cards.text: Un científico de datos quiere diagnósticos detallados; un cliente, un motivo breve y qué puede hacer; un auditor, documentación. Diseña las explicaciones pensando en quién las va a leer.

deep.x: Explanations should be designed for their audience and purpose. One model may need several explanation layers.

items.b: plain reason, how to change it

deep.x: Levels of detail

items: Global explanations: what drives the model
User message: short reason and next steps

deep.x: Example for a customer

"We couldn't approve this loan because your current debt payments are high relative to income. Reducing monthly debt by about €200 or adding a co-applicant may change the outcome. You can ask for a human review."
Model cards
Introduced by Google researchers in 2019, model cards document intended use, performance across groups, limitations and ethical considerations: explanations at the system level.
Over-detailed explanations can overwhelm users; studies find people prefer short, contrastive explanations ("why this rather than that").

cards.title: Las explicaciones generan confianza

items: Muestra lo seguro que está el modelo

cards.text: La gente confía más en las recomendaciones de la IA y las usa más cuando las entiende, pero también puede fiarse en exceso de una explicación que suena segura. Las buenas explicaciones también muestran la incertidumbre.

deep.x: Explanations can increase appropriate trust, helping people know when to rely on AI and when to question it. But persuasive explanations can also create false confidence.

items: accept wrong outputs because they sound convincing

deep.x: Research findings

Several studies found that adding explanations sometimes made people accept AI recommendations more often, including wrong ones. Showing uncertainty and evidence works better than confident narratives.
Good practice
Calibration
A calibrated model's confidence matches reality: among predictions at 80% confidence, about 80% are right. Calibration makes confidence scores meaningful for users.
The goal isn't maximum trust but the right amount of trust.

cards.title: Obligatorio en algunos casos
cards.text: El RGPD da a las personas afectadas por decisiones significativas basadas únicamente en el tratamiento automatizado el derecho a recibir información significativa sobre la lógica aplicada. El Reglamento de IA añade obligaciones de transparencia para los sistemas de alto riesgo.

deep.x: Several legal frameworks require explanations or transparency for AI-assisted decisions.

items: AI Act: transparency and instructions for high-risk systems
Consumer credit rules: reasons for refusal

deep.x: The AI Act's right to explanation

Article 86 gives people affected by decisions based on high-risk AI systems, with legal or similarly significant effects, the right to clear and meaningful explanations of the AI's role and the main elements of the decision.
Consumer credit
The EU's revised Consumer Credit Directive (2023) gives consumers the right to request human intervention and an explanation of creditworthiness assessments involving automated processing.
Practical compliance
Design explanation capability from the start: log inputs and outputs, record model versions, and prepare templates for customer explanations.
The US Equal Credit Opportunity Act has required "adverse action notices" stating reasons for credit refusals since the 1970s, shaping how credit models are built.

quiz.explain: SHAP atribuye una predicción concreta a sus características.

quiz.q: «Tu préstamo se aprobaría si tu deuda fuera 3000 € menor» es una…
quiz.explain: Describe el cambio más pequeño que invierte el resultado.

quiz.q: Un clasificador de huskies que se basa en la nieve del fondo demuestra…
options: Un atajo oculto que revelan las herramientas de explicación
quiz.explain: Los mapas de saliencia pusieron al descubierto la pista equivocada.

lessons.title: IA en los dispositivos
lessons.summary: Ejecutar modelos en móviles, cámaras y microcontroladores.

cards.title: IA en el borde
cards.text: La IA en el borde (edge AI) consiste en ejecutar los modelos donde se generan los datos: en un móvil, una cámara, un coche o un sensor, en lugar de enviarlo todo a la nube.

deep.x: Edge AI processes data close to where it's generated, from sensors and cameras to phones and industrial controllers. It reduces dependence on network connections and central servers.
The spectrum
Examples
Hybrid systems
Many systems split work: the device handles fast, private, simple tasks and sends only summaries or hard cases to the cloud.

steps: Sends only events or uncertain cases

deep.x: As chips improve, more AI moves to the edge; the cloud remains for the largest models and fleet-wide learning.

cards.title: ¿Por qué ejecutar en local?
cards.text: Cuatro motivos: velocidad (sin ida y vuelta por la red), privacidad (los datos nunca salen), coste (sin tarifas por llamada) y fiabilidad (funciona sin conexión).

deep.x: Edge deployment is chosen for specific benefits. Each matters differently by use case.

items.b: braking in a car can't wait for the cloud
video and audio stay at home

deep.x: Bandwidth
A single HD camera produces several megabits per second continuously. Sending only events ("person detected at 21:03") instead of raw video cuts bandwidth by orders of magnitude.

v.unit: data sent per day, GB (one camera)

deep.x: Regulation
Processing sensitive data locally can simplify GDPR compliance, since less personal data is transferred or stored centrally.
Trade-offs
Local processing means managing hardware, updates and security across many devices, which can be harder than managing one cloud service.
Choose the edge when speed, privacy or connectivity matter more than raw model power.

cards.title: Hacer pequeños los modelos
cards.text: Los modelos para el borde se reducen con cuantización (menos bits por peso), poda (eliminar conexiones poco importantes) y destilación (entrenar a un alumno pequeño para que copie a un profesor grande).

deep.x: Edge devices have limited memory, compute and energy, so models are compressed while keeping as much accuracy as possible.

items.b: remove near-zero weights or whole channels

deep.x: Knowledge distillation

Proposed by Hinton and colleagues in 2015, distillation trains a small model to match a large model's full output probabilities, not just correct labels. The "soft" probabilities carry extra information about similarities between classes.

steps: Small student learns to match them

deep.x: Results
Tools
TensorFlow Lite (LiteRT), ONNX Runtime, Core ML and PyTorch's ExecuTorch convert and optimise models for phones and embedded devices.
Small language models distilled from larger ones now run on phones, handling summarisation and smart replies offline.

cards.title: Aceleradores

items.l: pico de la Coral Edge TPU

cards.text: Chips pequeños como la Coral Edge TPU de Google o los motores neuronales de los móviles ejecutan redes neuronales de forma eficiente con unos pocos vatios. Una Coral TPU puede ejecutar un detector de objetos a decenas de fotogramas por segundo.

deep.x: Edge accelerators are specialised chips for neural network operations, delivering far more operations per watt than general CPUs.
TOPS
Edge chips are rated in TOPS: trillions of operations per second, usually at 8-bit precision. TOPS per watt is the key efficiency measure.
Constraints
Accelerators often support only certain operations and data types; models may need conversion and quantisation to run fully on the chip. Unsupported layers fall back to the slower CPU.
Choosing
Consider performance, power, software support, model compatibility, availability and cost. For home camera detection, a small accelerator often suffices.
Specs are only part of the story: software support and model compatibility decide real-world speed.

cards.title: Una cámara inteligente en casa

steps: Detector de objetos en esa zona

cards.text: Un NVR doméstico como Frigate usa primero una detección de movimiento barata, luego ejecuta el detector de objetos solo en los fotogramas con movimiento y solo avisa por los objetos que te interesan, como personas de noche.

deep.x: Frigate is an open-source network video recorder that runs object detection locally, integrating with Home Assistant. Its pipeline avoids wasting compute on empty frames.

steps: Object detector on regions with motion

deep.x: Smart filtering

items.b: only alert in the driveway, not the street

deep.x: Detector options
Frigate supports accelerators like Google Coral, Intel OpenVINO on integrated GPUs, NVIDIA GPUs and others, and models like YOLO variants.
Beyond detection
Newer features include face recognition, licence plate recognition and semantic search over recorded events using embeddings, all locally.
Running detection only where motion is found lets a modest home server handle many cameras that would overwhelm it if every frame were analysed.

cards.title: TinyML
cards.text: Incluso microcontroladores que cuestan unos pocos euros pueden ejecutar modelos diminutos: detección de palabras de activación, reconocimiento de gestos, detección de anomalías de vibración, todo con batería.

deep.x: TinyML runs machine learning on microcontrollers with kilobytes of memory and milliwatts of power, enabling AI in battery-powered sensors that last months or years.
Examples
Workflow

steps: Train small model on a computer

deep.x: Tools
TensorFlow Lite for Microcontrollers (now LiteRT), Edge Impulse and vendor toolkits help build models for chips like ESP32, Arduino Nano 33 BLE and STM32.

items.b: cheap Wi-Fi microcontroller, popular in home projects

deep.x: TinyML brings intelligence to places with no power socket and no network.

cards.title: Modelos de lenguaje en el dispositivo
cards.text: Los móviles y portátiles ya ejecutan pequeños modelos de lenguaje en local para resúmenes, respuestas inteligentes y dictado. Las peticiones más grandes se pueden seguir enviando a la nube.

deep.x: Small language models, typically 1–8 billion parameters and quantised, now run on phones and laptops. They handle summarisation, rewriting, smart replies and transcription locally.

steps: If too complex: route to cloud with permission

deep.x: Private cloud tiers
Some platforms send harder requests to secure cloud servers designed so the provider can't access data, combining local and cloud processing.
Running models yourself
Limits
A laptop with 32 GB of unified memory can run quantised models in the 30-billion-parameter range at usable speeds.

cards.title: Actualizar los modelos del borde
cards.text: Los dispositivos sobre el terreno necesitan nuevas versiones del modelo a medida que los datos derivan. Las actualizaciones se envían de forma inalámbrica (OTA), a menudo probándolas antes en un pequeño grupo de dispositivos.

deep.x: Edge models must be updated as data drifts, bugs are found or new features are needed. Over-the-air (OTA) updates deliver new versions safely across fleets.

steps: Test on a few devices: canary

deep.x: Challenges

x: Devices differ in hardware and software versions
Intermittent connectivity
Limited storage for multiple model versions
Security: updates must be signed to prevent tampering

deep.x: Collecting feedback
Edge devices can send back anonymised statistics or hard examples (with consent) to improve the next model version.
Treat edge AI as a fleet to manage, not a one-time installation.

cards.title: Aprendizaje federado

steps: El modelo central va a los equipos

cards.text: En lugar de recoger los datos de todo el mundo, los dispositivos entrenan en local y envían solo actualizaciones de pesos a un servidor central, que las combina. Los teclados de los móviles lo usan para mejorar las sugerencias sin subir lo que escribes.

deep.x: Federated learning, introduced by Google researchers in 2016–17, trains a shared model across many devices without collecting raw data centrally. Devices compute updates on local data; a server aggregates them.
Uses

items.b: learns from typing without uploading text
train on patient data that can't leave each hospital

deep.x: Privacy isn't automatic
Model updates can still leak information. Techniques like secure aggregation (server sees only the sum) and differential privacy (adding noise) strengthen protection.
Challenges

x: Devices have uneven, non-representative data
Communication costs
Devices drop in and out

deep.x: Google's Gboard keyboard was one of the first large-scale deployments of federated learning.

cards.title: Los límites del borde
cards.text: Los dispositivos pequeños tienen memoria, batería y margen térmico limitados. Los modelos del borde son menos capaces que los grandes modelos en la nube, así que muchos sistemas combinan ambos.

deep.x: Edge devices face hard physical limits: memory, compute, battery and heat. A phone can't dissipate the hundreds of watts a data-centre GPU uses.
Consequences

x: Smaller, less capable models
Shorter context and simpler tasks
Thermal throttling during sustained use
Fragmented hardware makes deployment complex

deep.x: Hybrid patterns

items: Split models across device and server

deep.x: Choosing wisely
The best systems use each where it's strongest.

quiz.q: Entrenar un modelo pequeño para que imite a uno grande se llama…
quiz.explain: El alumno aprende de las salidas del profesor.

quiz.q: ¿Por qué un sistema de cámaras doméstico ejecuta la detección en local?
options: Velocidad, privacidad y sin cuotas de la nube
La nube no puede detectar personas
quiz.explain: El procesamiento local es rápido, privado y barato.

quiz.q: En el aprendizaje federado, ¿qué sale del dispositivo?
quiz.explain: Los datos en bruto se quedan en local; solo se comparten las actualizaciones.

lessons.title: Robots y coches autónomos
lessons.summary: IA que se mueve por el mundo físico.

cards.title: Percibir, pensar, actuar
cards.text: Todo robot ejecuta el mismo bucle: los sensores miden el mundo, el software decide qué hacer y los motores lo ejecutan. Luego vuelve a percibir para ver qué ha cambiado.

deep.x: Robotics closes the loop between perception and action. Control loops run many times per second: a robot arm's motor controllers may update hundreds or thousands of times per second, while planning runs slower.
Layers of control

items: Task planning: what to do, seconds
Motion planning: how to move, tenths of a second

deep.x: Why robotics is hard

Unlike chatbots, robots face physics: uncertainty in sensing, slippery objects, delays, wear and the cost of mistakes. Moravec's paradox again: picking up a cup is harder for AI than writing an essay.
Feedback
Closed-loop control constantly corrects using sensor feedback, like a thermostat or cruise control.
The word "robot" comes from Karel Čapek's 1920 play *R.U.R.*, from the Czech *robota*, meaning forced labour.

cards.title: Sensores
cards.text: Los robots y los coches combinan sensores porque cada uno tiene puntos débiles: las cámaras ven el color pero sufren en la oscuridad, el radar ve a través de la lluvia pero con menos detalle y el lidar mide distancias precisas con láseres.

deep.x: Each sensor type has strengths and weaknesses; sensor fusion combines them for a reliable picture.

items.b: colour, signs, texture, weak in dark and glare
speed and distance through rain and fog, low detail
precise 3D shape, costly, affected by heavy rain

deep.x: Other sensors

x: **IMU**: accelerometers and gyroscopes measure motion and tilt
**GPS**: global position, metres, or centimetres with corrections
**Wheel encoders**: distance travelled
**Force and touch sensors**: grip and collisions

deep.x: Sensor fusion
Algorithms like Kalman filters combine noisy measurements from different sensors, weighting each by reliability, to estimate position and motion better than any single sensor.
Camera-only vs multi-sensor
Tesla pursues camera-only driving; Waymo and most robotaxi companies combine cameras, lidar and radar.
Redundancy matters: when one sensor is blinded, others keep the robot safe.

cards.title: Localización y mapeo
cards.text: Para moverse, un robot tiene que saber dónde está. El SLAM (localización y mapeo simultáneos) construye un mapa de un espacio desconocido mientras sigue la posición del robot dentro de él. Los robots aspiradores lo hacen.

deep.x: SLAM solves a chicken-and-egg problem: to build a map you need to know where you are, and to know where you are you need a map. SLAM estimates both together, refining as the robot moves.
Loop closure
When a robot returns to a place it has seen before, recognising it lets the algorithm correct accumulated drift across the whole map.
Types

items.b: precise geometry, robot vacuums and warehouses

deep.x: Everyday SLAM
Robot vacuums map your home to clean systematically; phones use visual-inertial SLAM for augmented reality, placing virtual furniture in your room.
NASA's Mars rovers use visual odometry, a SLAM relative, to measure their own movement over rocky terrain where wheels slip.

cards.title: Niveles de conducción automatizada

items: Nivel 5: en todas partes, sin conductor
Nivel 4: sin conductor en zonas definidas
Nivel 3: conduce el coche, humano atento

cards.text: La SAE define seis niveles, del 0 (sin automatización) al 5 (conduce en cualquier lugar sin una persona). La mayoría de los coches que se venden hoy ofrecen el nivel 2: el coche gira y frena, pero el conductor debe supervisar constantemente.

deep.x: The SAE J3016 standard defines six levels. The key distinction is who's responsible for monitoring the road.

items: Level 4: no human within defined areas
Level 3: car drives, human takes over on request
Level 2: car steers and brakes, human supervises

deep.x: The responsibility line
Level 3 in Europe
Since 2022, some cars have been approved in Germany and elsewhere for Level 3 on motorways at limited speeds, where the driver may legally look away until asked to take over.
Misunderstanding
Marketing names like "Autopilot" have led drivers to over-trust Level 2 systems; regulators have investigated crashes where drivers weren't paying attention.

deep.r: Most cars sold today are Level 2: you must keep watching the road

deep.x: Level 2 is driver assistance; true self-driving begins at Level 4.

cards.title: Robotaxis
cards.text: Hay servicios de taxis sin conductor en varias ciudades de EE. UU. y China, como Waymo en Phoenix y San Francisco. Son de nivel 4: sin conductor, pero solo dentro de zonas cartografiadas con cuidado.

deep.x: Level 4 robotaxis operate without a safety driver within defined areas ("operational design domains"), carefully mapped and tested, with remote assistance available.

events.l: Waymo expands, hundreds of thousands of paid rides a week

deep.x: Major players

items.b: Phoenix, San Francisco, Los Angeles and more

deep.x: Safety evidence
Waymo has published data from tens of millions of driverless miles reporting substantially fewer injury crashes than human benchmarks in the same cities. Independent analysis continues.
Challenges

x: Expanding to new cities, weather and road cultures
Cost of vehicles and sensors
Rare scenarios and public trust
Regulation that differs by country

deep.x: Robotaxis rely on remote human assistants who can give guidance in confusing situations, though they don't drive the car directly.

cards.title: La larga cola
cards.text: Conducir es sobre todo rutina, pero las situaciones raras son infinitas: un colchón en la autopista, un policía que te indica que pases con el semáforo en rojo. Gestionar la larga cola de sucesos raros es lo más difícil de la autonomía.

deep.x: The long tail is the vast number of rare situations that each occur seldom but together happen constantly. Getting from 99% to 99.9999% reliability is far harder than reaching 99%.
Examples
Strategies

x: Massive simulation of rare scenarios
Collecting and labelling unusual events from fleets
Conservative behaviour when uncertain: slow down, stop safely
Remote assistance for confusing situations

deep.x: Why it matters elsewhere
Every AI deployment has a long tail: customer requests nobody anticipated, documents in odd formats, unusual machine failures. Plan for exceptions.
Reliability is measured by how a system handles the weird cases, not the typical ones.

cards.title: Robots industriales
cards.text: Las fábricas llevan décadas usando brazos robóticos para soldar, pintar y montar. La IA añade visión para que puedan coger piezas desordenadas, inspeccionar la calidad y trabajar con más seguridad cerca de las personas.

deep.x: The first industrial robot, Unimate, began work at a General Motors plant in 1961, handling hot die-cast parts. Today millions of industrial robots work worldwide.
AI adds flexibility
Traditional robots repeat precise programmed motions in fixed cells. AI vision lets them handle variation: picking mixed items from bins, inspecting surfaces, adapting to part positions.
Cobots
Collaborative robots work alongside people with force limits and sensors, taking on repetitive or ergonomic-risk tasks while humans handle judgement.
Warehouses
Logistics uses robots to move shelves, sort parcels and pick items. Amazon reported operating over a million robots in its fulfilment network by 2025.
Portugal's car and component factories, such as Autoeuropa in Palmela, use hundreds of robots for welding and painting.

cards.title: Aprender habilidades robóticas
cards.text: Los nuevos enfoques entrenan robots con demostraciones, simulación y grandes modelos que conectan el lenguaje y la visión con acciones: «pon la taza roja en el fregadero».

deep.x: New approaches aim to give robots general skills rather than hand-programmed routines.
Vision-language-action models

Models like Google DeepMind's RT-2 (2023) combine web-trained vision-language knowledge with robot data, so a robot can follow instructions involving concepts it never saw in robot training, like "move the banana to the picture of Germany".
Humanoids
Many companies are developing humanoid robots for factories and homes, betting that human-shaped robots fit human environments. Practical deployment is still early.
The data problem
Unlike text, robot data must be collected physically. Large shared datasets like Open X-Embodiment pool data from many labs and robot types.
Robotics may follow language AI's path once large, diverse datasets exist; that's the race today.

cards.title: La seguridad, lo primero

items: Límite de velocidad junto a personas

cards.text: Los robots físicos pueden herir a las personas, así que necesitan límites de velocidad cerca de humanos, paradas de emergencia, zonas valladas o sensores de fuerza, y certificación conforme a las normas de seguridad de máquinas.

deep.x: Physical robots can cause injury, so safety standards and engineering controls are mandatory.

items: Speed and force limits near people

deep.x: Standards

items.b: applies from 2027, covers AI-based safety functions
high-risk if AI is a safety component

deep.x: Collaborative safety
Cobots use power and force limiting: if they touch a person, contact forces stay below thresholds set by body region, so they stop before causing harm.
Safety vs AI uncertainty
AI components can behave unpredictably, so safety functions are often handled by separate, simpler, certified systems that can override AI decisions.
The EU's new Machinery Regulation explicitly addresses machines with self-evolving behaviour, a first for AI-driven equipment.

cards.title: Drones y agricultura

steps: La IA detecta zonas con problemas

cards.text: Los drones cartografían campos, cuentan plantas y detectan enfermedades, mientras que los tractores autónomos siguen rutas GPS con precisión de centímetros. La agricultura de precisión usa menos fertilizante y agua porque trata solo donde hace falta.

deep.x: Precision agriculture uses sensors, drones and AI to treat fields according to local need rather than uniformly, saving inputs and protecting the environment.
Technologies
Savings
"See and spray" systems that target individual weeds have reported herbicide reductions of 60–90% in trials compared with blanket spraying.
In Portugal
Alentejo olive groves, vineyards and irrigated crops use sensors and satellite data to manage water carefully, crucial during droughts. Copernicus Sentinel data is freely available.
Drones can count trees, estimate fruit yield and even pollinate in experiments, though bees remain far more efficient.

quiz.q: ¿Qué sensor mide distancias 3D precisas con láseres?
quiz.explain: El lidar usa pulsos láser para medir distancias.

quiz.q: La mayoría de los coches con asistencia a la conducción que se venden hoy son de nivel SAE…
quiz.explain: El nivel 2 gira y frena, pero necesita supervisión constante.

quiz.q: ¿Qué hace el SLAM?
options: Construye un mapa mientras sigue la posición del robot en él
quiz.explain: Localización y mapeo simultáneos.

lessons.title: Hacia dónde va la IA
lessons.summary: Agentes, debates sobre la AGI y qué conviene seguir.

cards.title: De los chatbots a los agentes
cards.text: Los agentes no solo responden: planifican y actúan. Buscan en la web, usan software, escriben y ejecutan código y luego comprueban el resultado. Trabajan en bucles hacia un objetivo.

deep.x: An AI agent uses a model in a loop with tools and memory to pursue goals over multiple steps: planning, acting, observing results and adjusting.
What agents can do

items: Research and summarise across many sources

deep.x: Design questions

items.b: how much they do without asking

deep.x: Reliability
Errors compound over steps: a 95% success rate per step gives only about 60% over ten steps. Better models, verification steps and human checkpoints address this.
Agents are most useful today for well-scoped tasks with clear success checks, like code with tests.

cards.title: Modelos multimodales
cards.text: Los modelos más recientes manejan texto, imágenes, audio y vídeo en un solo sistema. Puedes enseñar la foto de una pieza rota, hacer una pregunta por voz y recibir un diagrama.

deep.x: Multimodal models process and generate several types of data, text, images, audio and video, in a single model, rather than chaining separate systems.
Capabilities

items.b: describe and answer questions about clips

deep.x: Business uses

x: Field technicians photographing equipment and asking for repair steps
Reading scanned contracts and invoices directly
Analysing call recordings for quality and sentiment
Generating product images and marketing variants

deep.x: Why one model helps
A single model keeps context across modalities: it can relate what's in an image to what's said in a meeting, which separate systems struggle to do.
Real-time voice and video assistants can now see through a phone camera and talk back with natural interruptions.

cards.title: ¿Qué es la AGI?
cards.text: La inteligencia artificial general (AGI) suele referirse a una IA capaz de hacer la mayoría de las tareas cognitivas tan bien como una persona competente. No hay una definición ni una prueba acordadas, y los expertos discrepan mucho sobre cuándo llegará, o si llegará.

deep.x: AGI has many definitions: AI matching humans at most economically valuable work; AI that can learn any intellectual task a human can; or simply systems far more general than today's. Without agreement on the definition, timelines are hard to compare.

items: Learning: learns new tasks like humans
Levels: graded scales of capability and autonomy

deep.x: Expert views vary

Surveys of AI researchers give a wide spread of predictions, with medians moving earlier in recent years. Some leaders of AI labs suggest highly capable systems within years; many researchers expect longer or doubt the framing.
Jagged frontier
Current AI is "jagged": superhuman at some tasks (broad knowledge, coding contests) and weak at others (reliable long tasks, physical common sense). Progress doesn't arrive evenly.
Why it matters
Highly general AI would transform economies, science and security, which is why governments and labs debate safety, governance and how to share benefits.
Rather than waiting for an "AGI moment", track concrete capabilities and their real-world effects.

cards.title: Escalar frente a ideas nuevas
cards.text: Algunos investigadores esperan que más datos y más cálculo sigan dando resultados; otros creen que hacen falta ideas nuevas para lograr un razonamiento fiable, memoria y aprendizaje con pocos ejemplos. La mayoría espera un poco de ambas cosas.

deep.x: Since 2018, much progress came from scaling: bigger models, more data, more compute. Debate continues about how far that path goes.

items: need breakthroughs in reasoning, memory, learning efficiency

deep.x: What's actually happening
Labs combine both: scaling pre-training, plus new methods like reinforcement learning for reasoning, longer test-time thinking, better data curation and tool use.
Open problems
Constraints

x: High-quality data is finite
Compute and energy costs grow steeply
Chip supply and power grids limit expansion

deep.x: Efficiency improvements mean a given capability gets much cheaper each year: some analyses found the cost per token for a given performance level fell more than tenfold per year.

cards.title: IA para la ciencia
cards.text: La IA ya está acelerando la investigación. AlphaFold, de DeepMind, predijo la forma 3D de más de 200 millones de proteínas, y sus creadores compartieron el Premio Nobel de Química de 2024.

deep.x: AI is becoming a scientific tool across fields, from predicting molecular structures to controlling fusion plasma.
Other examples

items.b: DeepMind's GNoME proposed millions of crystal structures
AI models rival traditional forecasts at a fraction of the compute
RL controlled plasma in a tokamak

deep.x: Weather forecasting

Models like GraphCast and the ECMWF's AIFS produce 10-day forecasts in minutes on a single machine, versus hours on supercomputers for traditional models, with competitive accuracy. ECMWF began running AIFS operationally in 2025.

items: about a minute on one machine

deep.x: Limits
Predictions still need experimental validation; AI can propose, but labs confirm. Many generated "new materials" haven't been synthesised yet.
Demis Hassabis and John Jumper shared the 2024 Chemistry Nobel with David Baker, who designs new proteins computationally.

cards.title: Empleo y trabajo

items: revisar lo que hace la IA

cards.text: La IA cambia las tareas antes de sustituir empleos. Las tareas rutinarias de redacción, resumen y programación son las que cambian más rápido; los puestos pasan a centrarse en el criterio, las relaciones y la supervisión de lo que produce la IA.

deep.x: AI automates tasks, not whole jobs, at first. Most jobs are bundles of tasks; some get automated, some augmented, some untouched.
Evidence so far

Studies of customer support agents (2023) found AI assistants raised productivity by about 14% on average, and by about 34% for less experienced workers. Consultants using AI did better on tasks within its capability but worse on tasks outside it.
Exposure
The IMF estimated in 2024 that around 40% of global employment is exposed to AI, rising to about 60% in advanced economies, with roughly half of exposed jobs likely to benefit from complementarity.
Skills that rise in value
Workers who learn to use AI well are likely to outpace those who don't.

cards.title: Modelos abiertos frente a cerrados

items: mal uso más difícil de controlar

cards.text: Algunos modelos se publican abiertamente para que cualquiera pueda ejecutarlos y modificarlos; otros solo están disponibles a través de una API. Los modelos abiertos favorecen la investigación y la privacidad; los cerrados facilitan el control del mal uso.

deep.x: "Open" in AI usually means open weights: the trained parameters are downloadable. Fully open source would also include training data and code, which is rarer.
Examples

items.b: mostly closed frontier models, some open releases

deep.x: For enterprises
Open-weight models allow private deployment, fine-tuning and cost control; closed models offer convenience and often the highest capability. Many companies use both through a gateway.
The debate
Open models accelerate research and reduce dependence on a few firms; critics worry about misuse of powerful capabilities once weights are released, since safeguards can be removed.
The "DeepSeek moment" in January 2025, when an efficient open-weight reasoning model matched leading closed models on benchmarks, briefly wiped hundreds of billions off chip-maker valuations.

cards.title: Límites de energía y cálculo
cards.text: Cada nueva generación necesita más chips, electricidad y refrigeración. El suministro eléctrico, la producción de chips y el coste pueden limitar la velocidad a la que escala la IA.

deep.x: Frontier AI's appetite for chips and electricity is growing rapidly. Large training clusters now draw hundreds of megawatts, and companies plan gigawatt-scale campuses.
Bottlenecks
Responses

x: Locating data centres near abundant renewable or nuclear power
Long-term power purchase agreements
More efficient chips, models and inference techniques
Running flexible workloads when power is cheap and green

deep.x: Portugal's angle
Portugal's renewable electricity share, Atlantic subsea cables and available land have attracted large data-centre projects, raising questions about grid capacity and water.
Physical infrastructure, not just algorithms, may set the pace of AI progress.

cards.title: Mantenerse informado
cards.text: Este campo cambia cada mes. Hábitos útiles: prueba las herramientas tú mismo, sigue unas pocas fuentes fiables y juzga las afirmaciones por las demostraciones y las pruebas, no por el bombo.

deep.x: AI moves fast enough that knowledge from a year ago can be outdated. A sustainable habit beats chasing every headline.

items: Read primary sources for big claims

deep.x: Judging claims
Build your own evaluation set
Keep a small set of real tasks from your work. When a new model appears, run it on your tasks and compare quality, speed and cost. This beats leaderboard watching.
Signals vs noise
Hype cycles and doom cycles alternate. Focus on deployed capabilities, adoption data and measured productivity effects.
Benchmarks saturate quickly: tests designed to last years are often near-solved within months of release.

cards.title: Lo que sigue siendo humano
cards.text: Decidir qué problemas importan, sopesar ventajas e inconvenientes, asumir responsabilidades y generar confianza entre personas sigue siendo trabajo humano, ahora con asistentes muy potentes.

deep.x: As AI handles more cognitive tasks, the distinctly human contributions shift towards purpose, judgement, accountability and connection.
Human accountability
Law and ethics hold people and organisations responsible, not tools. Someone must own each AI system's outcomes, especially in high-stakes decisions.
Working with AI
The most effective pattern is often a partnership: AI drafts, explores and checks; humans frame problems, evaluate and decide.
Learning still matters
Expertise lets you spot AI's mistakes, ask better questions and know what good looks like. Learning, like this app encourages, becomes more valuable, not less.
The question isn't whether AI can do a task, but how people and AI together can do it best.

quiz.q: ¿Qué distingue a un agente de IA de un chatbot básico?
options: Planifica y realiza acciones con herramientas para lograr un objetivo
quiz.explain: Los agentes actúan en bucles usando herramientas.

quiz.q: ¿Qué hizo AlphaFold?
options: Predecir la estructura 3D de las proteínas
quiz.explain: Predijo más de 200 millones de estructuras de proteínas.

quiz.q: ¿Hay una fecha acordada para la AGI?
quiz.explain: No hay consenso ni sobre la definición ni sobre los plazos.
